A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FMG work despite the changed title. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and matching methods and experiments support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original QM9 and GEOM generation results, property-conditioned generation, a synthetic chirality experiment and ablation studies.

after.justification: V2 retains original FMG experiments and adds energy evaluations, field-parameter sensitivity results and computational profiling.

M1.justification: V1 Section 3 and v2 Section 4 retain the atom/bond RBF fields, diffusion objective and schedules, classifier-free guidance, principal-component alignment, U-Net and graph-extraction procedure. The corresponding implementation appendices retain the core architecture and parameter values.

E1.justification: Both evaluate QM9, GEOM, property-conditioned QM9 generation and the same synthetic set of 48 chiral molecules. GEOM-Drugs is the renamed retained coverage. Energy, sensitivity and computational analyses extend evaluation within these datasets rather than introducing another molecular task or domain.

E2.justification: V2 adds JODO to the basic-property, graph-quality and conformational comparisons in Tables 1, 2, 4 and 5. The existing comparator set is otherwise retained. GNN becoming GDM-AUG in the chirality figure identifies the existing comparator rather than adding one.

E3.justification: V2 adds MMFF and GFN2-xTB energy-distribution metrics and removes novelty evaluation. Section 5 and Appendix H restrict generated bond lengths and angles to the data range, whereas v1's metric description includes the generated and data ranges. New sensitivity and profiling experiments also introduce parameter sweeps, timing procedures and memory-measurement settings.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained rotation, guidance and bond-extraction ablations, v2 Appendix C tests extraction robustness across RBF variances and grid resolutions. Table 4 adds the effect of atom-count guidance on xTB energy distance. Appendix J adds extensive runtime, memory and channel-scaling analyses.

E5.justification: FMG's QM9 results retain means and standard deviations across three runs of 10,000 samples, while GEOM results remain point estimates. The added energy columns extend the existing reporting practice; neither version introduces seed lists, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds energy, sensitivity and computational results plus JODO entries, and removes novelty scores. Retained values also change: QM9 EDM/MiDi MST changes from 0.57/0.55 to 0.55/0.57, and implicit-hydrogen FMG GEOM validity changes from 80.8% to 80.0%. FMG's GEOM bond-angle distance changes from 1.99 to 1.00 under revised filtering, so this does not establish a same-setting improvement. Conditional-generation and original ablation results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix A.3's distance-and-angle invariance argument is retained and substantially extended. V2 Section 3 and Appendix B add formal propositions, an SE(n)/E(n) lemma, the diffusion-distribution invariance derivation and the claimed O(n^4) requirement for chirality features. Appendix J additionally derives field-computation scaling bounds.

C1.justification: V1 already claims competitive field-based generation and chirality sensitivity. V2 makes formal limitations of E(3)-equivariant generation central to its title and contributions, and adds the substantive claim that chirality-sensitive invariant features require at least four positions and quartic scaling. Its contrast with prior methods is also qualified through recognition of existing chirality-aware approaches.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning molecule shape, field volume, computational feasibility and transfer to other 3D tasks. Appendix A.1 interprets energy discrepancies through atom-count conditioning and hypothesizes benefits from finer conditioning. Appendix C distinguishes extraction sensitivity tests from unperformed end-to-end diffusion hyperparameter ablations.

D1.justification: V2 adds a stated FMG code-access link, explicitly documents the equal conditional-generator/classifier training split, specifies 17/91 atom-count conditioning bins and supplies profiling settings. These are additional disclosures; the core U-Net, optimizer, training budgets, hardware and extraction parameters were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: V2 adds a dedicated discussion of chirality-aware work, including Adams, Liu, Jing, and Luo and Ji, distinguishing conditional conformer generation from joint graph/conformation generation. It sharpens the comparison with VoxMol and expands graph-diffusion and transformer coverage. This substantially revises positioning beyond v1's broad description of chirality as previously omitted.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten around chirality and symmetry. V2 introduces a dedicated theory section, streamlines existing method explanations, moves conditional-experiment details into the appendix and reorganizes the appendices around theory, implementation and complexity.

P2.justification: V2 switches the main text to a single-column layout, merges cross-dataset benchmark tables and splits the conformational table. Figure 2 combines sampling and extraction illustrations, while the bond-optimization illustration moves to the appendix. New energy, sensitivity and profiling plots accompany substantially redesigned 3D sample displays.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's limited characterization of conformation energies, parameter sensitivity and computational feasibility through new comparisons and diagnostic experiments. These expose concrete weaknesses and applicability limits, while expanded related work improves novelty positioning. The unchanged method becomes substantially easier to assess critically. Removed novelty results and changed bond-length/angle filtering reduce evaluation continuity, but do not outweigh these gains.
